newsitem.title: UK: UK J-block producing gas despite litigation - Philli.
newsitem.headline: UK J-block producing gas despite litigation - Philli.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co is producing gas from its Judy field in the North Sea J-block despite continued litigation between the field owners and Enron Corp, the gas buyer, a Phillips spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman told journalists that production will continue for about another week.

Enron announced on November 13 that it intended to take gas from Judy to prove that Phillips is capable of producing at a rate of 300 million cubic feet per day (mcfd) and that Enron's facilities at Teesside can handle that volume.
The first gas nominations started on November 18 and testing will continue for around one more week.
The two sides hope to achieve production at the rate of 300 mcfd for at least three days.
The testing will make no difference to the litigation between the two sides, the spokesman for Phillips told journalists visiting a Tyneside shipyard.

Enron has a long-term "take-or-pay" contract to buy gas from J-block with producers Phillips (36.5 percent, operator), Agip (UK) Ltd (33 percent) and British Gas Exploration and Production Ltd (30.5 percent).

But it has told producers that because of a slump in prices on the U.K. spot market, it would not take delivery of gas before September 30, 1998. Enron also refused to agree a commissioning date, so seeking to defer the start of its take-or-pay obligations.

Phillips won a victory in the High Court in May when the court ruled that Enron could not refuse to agree a commissioning date. This ruling was overturned in the Court of Appeal in October, a decision which Phillips plans to appeal.
